A longtime admirer of Pike Place Market, Robin visited the Market on vacations and brought home treasures she has cherished over the years. Now, as a new Pike Place Market vendor, she is excited to create pieces for visitors to discover and cherish of their own. She creates nature-inspired watercolor paintings that celebrate the beauty of the natural world; a little bit of the trail and garden to bring into your everyday life. Her artwork is available as original paintings, prints, and cards. She also crafts and sells small-batch watercolor paints made from foraged, garden-grown, and thoughtfully sourced plants and earth pigments. Each color has a story. For example, a rich golden hue is made from marigold petals grown in my own garden. _page.text: Meet Me In The Market, The Singing Tour Guide - Pike Place Market Skip to content See Who's Open Parking & Directions Plan Your Visit About the Market Programs & Events Directory Market Map --> --> Your Market Day English Chinese (Simplified) English French German Hindi Russian Spanish --> show holiday graphics on home: false --> Home Directory Meet Me In The Market, The Singing Tour Guide Meet Me In The Market, The Singing Tour Guide Shop Now Davin will be on EU tour Oct 1-21 Join Seattle’s most acclaimed singing historian and frontman for The Staxx Brothers on a one-of-a-kind tour of Pike Place Market. For $25, the price of a local show, spend 90 minutes plus an encore with Davin Michael Stedman. In a small group visitors can now explore and experience the Market like never before. This is the only historic tour that culminates with an unplugged concert at the very same iconic busking locations where Pike Place greats like Brandi Carlile and Artis Spoonman made music history in the pages of Rolling Stone. As a bonus you will get a signed copy of Davin’s debut solo album, West Indian Rock, that includes his hit song “Free Your Mind” with Sly & Robbie, that landed him a distribution deal with Bob Marley’s label Tuff Gong International. This groundbreaking album, which is slated for worldwide release in Fall 2026, is available exclusively to people that join Davin on this tour.

The curated selection includes decks by local authors as well as designs and artwork spanning a wide range of themes and styles. Whether you’re searching for your first tarot deck or adding to an established collection, Tarot Crow is likely to have just what you need. For seasoned collectors, Corax also plans to introduce a buy, sell, and trade program, giving decks a second life and encouraging community among fellow tarot enthusiasts. In addition to tarot decks, the shop features Corax’s handmade, vegan candles, incense, bath bombs, and body oils. All products are crafted without synthetics and made with natural botanicals. Corax is particularly known for his scented creations inspired by the archetypes of the Major Arcana. Every item is produced locally, just down the street at his studio in Post Alley. Riccio’s Sausage Co. Shop Now About Us Built on generations of family tradition, Riccio’s Sausage Company brings a taste of Calabria to Pike Place Market. Owner Stanislao “Stano” Rodolfo Riccio uses techniques passed down through his family, making Riccio’s rotating selection of locally made sausages a must‑try for Market visitors. Stanislao emphasizes the importance of high‑quality, locally sourced ingredients, many of which are found right at the Market. These ingredients shine across a menu of sandwiches, housemade focaccia, pasta, vegetables, and other seasonal offerings. Guests can choose from hot or cold sandwiches: hot options feature a choice of sausage flavor (hot or mild Italian, or hot or mild Calabrian) paired with a variety of roasted and grilled vegetables and other toppings, while cold sandwiches highlight assorted cured meats served on fresh, house-made focaccia. At home with her newly adopted and anxious rescue pup, Pocket, Danielle set out to solve a familiar problem: finding a toy that could keep up with Pocket’s nervous energy. With just a scrap of leather and a hole punch, she made a pizza-shaped squeaky toy that kept Pocket entertained for hours. That moment sparked a new passion—creating better, longer-lasting gear for dogs and their people. What began as a homemade toy has grown into a full line of thoughtfully designed leashes, collars, and pet accessories. Every piece is built for durability, comfort, and real-life adventures—because Danielle believes the connection between you and your pup should be strong and beautiful. Ever feel obsessed with a color? For Natalie Menacho, it’s indigo—deep, rich, and full of magic. Who knew such a stunning hue could come from the green leaf of a perennial plant? Natalie is a multi-disciplinary artist based on Orcas Island. She began dyeing with indigo in 2016, captivated by its alchemical transformation, and took things a step further in 2024 by growing her own indigo. Using traditional shibori folding techniques and organic indigo-and-henna dyeing, she creates one-of-a-kind textiles that bring beauty and function into everyday life. Her ceramic work follows the same philosophy—hand built, functional pieces that blend wabi-sabi modernity with a touch of bohemian magic. Whether it’s a set of indigo-dyed napkins or a perfectly imperfect ceramic spoon rest, Natalie’s work is meant to be used, loved, and lived with. Using an orchard-to-glass approach, founders Nick and Holly focus on heritage cider apples rarely found in modern cider production, creating ciders that showcase the character and complexity of the fruit itself. The cidery began in 2017 after the pair discovered an antique cider press and started making cider for friends and family. What began as a passion project quickly grew into one of the most awarded cideries in the Pacific Northwest. Since 2019, Puget Sound Cider Company has earned more than 80 awards at regional, national, and international competitions, including honors from the Northwest Cider Cup, Great Lakes International Cider & Perry Competition, Portland International Cider Cup, and CiderCraft Awards. Very sorry for any inconvenience! About Us Tucked into the heart of Pike Place Market, Lonely Siren is a tavern style cocktail bar inspired by old waterfront dives, Portuguese hospitality, and the beautifully strange community that makes this neighborhood unlike anywhere else. This is a place for artists finishing a market day, chefs grabbing a late-night drink, musicians, fishermen, travelers who wandered in by accident, and locals who somehow always end up at the same corner of the bar. Good conversations happen here. So do great cocktails. Our menu celebrates the Atlantic coast with Portuguese wines, creative cocktails, petiscos, conservas, and seasonal dishes meant to be shared. We believe exceptional food and drinks don’t need white tablecloths—just honest hospitality and a room full of interesting people. Like Pike Place itself, Lonely Siren is a little weathered, a little unexpected, and full of stories waiting to be told. Come as you are. Stay longer than you planned Directions : T

We make dairy the long way, fermenting live cultures into fresh local milk, then churning it slow. Thick, tangy and alive with flavor. Every batch starts with intention. We’re not here to chase trends. We’re here to honour the craft we grew up with. To take something simple and do it properly. Hellenika is our way of keeping old techniques alive while making something new. Seasonal. Emotional. Tied to place. That place is here. Pike Place shapes everything we do. We steep MarketSpice tea into our mix when the grey sky rolls in. We use Sunny Honey when the bees are flying. We cook with neighbors at Atrium Kitchen because food should be shared, not just sold. The Greek cultures we use have been in our family for generations but, the flavors are born from this street, this city, this market. Nothing we make is static. That’s the beauty of cultured food. Founded in 2018 using a hundred-year-old multi-generational family recipe, we handcraft small batches of authentic Indian masala chai. Our chai uses carefully selected estate-grown Assamese black tea leaves, locally grown farm fresh organic lemongrass, ginger tubers, and fresh mint. We grind whole spices sourced from farmer-centric cooperatives. The result is an unmatched chai with multiple layers of flavors and experience. The tea is spice-filled, yet not spicy; sweetened though not sweet. We invite you to stop by when visiting Pike Place Market and “chai some”! Fantello Farmstead Creamery began in 1918 in Enumclaw and continues to use the same farm-to-table methods. The Fantellos make cheese that is truly handmade every step of the way, from milking the cows into cans and hand dumping the milk into the vats, pail by pail, to aging in on wooden boards to make cheese as pure as possible. They don’t use milk pumps or outsource milk from other farmers to make their cheese. Farmer Paul says that by being involved in every step, they have complete control over the final product. As a Hilltop Tacoma native, Juanita grew up seeing poverty first-hand and understands the importance of accessibility to fresh produce. When the family first started their urban farming journey, they found that they were selling many of their microgreens to chefs and the wealthy. Baby Chavs wants to change this perception and encourage healthy eating by making microgreens more approachable and versatile in every American household. Both their indoor and outdoor spaces are maximized to optimum efficiency. Their microgreens are practically soil free! Baby Chavs use mostly coco coir, the discarded fibers of coconuts, as a growing medium, along with a touch of soil to help with fertilizing. Coconut fibers contain nutrients optimal for plant growth. Owner Dave Alberg carefully cultivates a 20 acres orchard in Royal City, Washington, about 170 miles southwest of Seattle. Never sprayed with chemicals and pruned to a minimum, the original cherry trees Alberg planted in the 70s still produce fruit to this day. Alberg Cherry is known for having some of the very first Washington state cherries of the season and attributes this head-start to the warm weather east of the Cascade mountains. Their table is packed with bundles of cherries, apricots, apples, and pears when the season kicks off in early June. Don’t hesitate to swing by – the growing window for cherries is short and sweet – often wrapping up by the end of July! rows.name: Dot & Dimension
rows.blurb: Ritu Tilwani is the designer-printer-maker behind Dot and Dimension. She creates hand-carved linocut prints in her little home studio in Seattle.

_page.text: Dot & Dimension - Pike Place Market Skip to content See Who's Open Parking & Directions Plan Your Visit About the Market Programs & Events Directory Market Map --> --> Your Market Day English Chinese (Simplified) English French German Hindi Russian Spanish --> show holiday graphics on home: false --> Home Directory Dot & Dimension Dot & Dimension Shop Now About Us Ritu Tilwani is the designer-printer-maker behind Dot and Dimension. She creates hand-carved linocut prints in her little home studio in Seattle. A scuba diver, marine biology enthusiast, and an ocean advocate, she finds inspiration for her prints from the ocean. Most of her work is based on underwater pictures taken by her and her husband when they go diving together. Working with a monochrome palette, Ritu loves the challenge of creating depth and dimension while working with a single tone of color. She aspires to create art that is, “Striking yet calm, graphic yet organic at the same time”. About Us John Sollid is a block print artist in Pike Place Market who sells handcrafted colorful wall art, greeting cards, and children’s t-shirts. He has been selling his work in the Market since 1973. Before choosing art as his life’s passion, John was an English teacher for 6 years. John’s knowledge of art and his formal art training came from his father. John was born in a small town in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan near Lake Superior. He has lived in various parts of the country, including Idaho, before settling in Seattle in 1970. Find John Sollid in the Pike Place Market Craft Market on Mondays. Simple yet elegant design, unique textures, and bold color combinations make her happy. Amy grew up right here in the Seattle area, and she’s proud to be a Pike Place Market crafts vendor since 2018. She does not have a regular Market schedule; it changes throughout the year. Please email her if you’d like to find out when she’ll be at Pike Place Market. What is Cork Fabric? A Durable, Flexible Material Many Minter Goods items are made of cork fabric. This is a durable, flexible material with a really wonderful texture. It is comprised of a very thin layer of cork affixed to a fabric backing. The fabric backing makes it quite strong and durable, it will not tear. Using driftwood as well as beautiful hardwoods, Neptune Furniture offers rocking chairs, benches, footstools, cutting boards, firelighters wall plaques, and other astonishing one-of-a-kind items. Jim has lived and worked on Vashon Island for more than 30 years. The beach and the driftwood he finds there has always been Jim’s muse. Living on an island gifts him with an abundance of trees, rocks, and tides. Each day, new gifts of driftwood present themselves to be incorporated into Jim’s creations. Making functional art into a functional business is, in itself, an art all its own. Harnessing creativity and directing its flow are skills continually in development at Neptune Furniture. _page.text: Giant Shoe Museum - Pike Place Market Skip to content See Who's Open Parking & Directions Plan Your Visit About the Market Programs & Events Directory Market Map --> --> Your Market Day English Chinese (Simplified) English French German Hindi Russian Spanish --> show holiday graphics on home: false --> Home Directory Giant Shoe Museum Giant Shoe Museum About the Giant Shoe Museum Resembling an entrance to a circus sideshow, the Giant Shoe Museum is a flamboyant presence at Pike Place Market. While it is essentially a single exhibit wall, it occupies a sizable chunk outside Old Seattle Paperworks . The Museum displays part of the collection of Danny Eskenazi, who became obsessed with giant shoes after he’d learned that his grandfather had once owned a wingtip worn by Robert Wadlow, the world’s tallest man. Eskenazi offered $1,000 to anyone who could find that Wadlow shoe. It remains lost, but his efforts led to the discovery of the other shoes that are now displayed in the Museum. Visitors can drop quarters into coin boxes, peer through stereoscope-style viewing slots, and are rewarded with views of various giant shoes, including another size 37 brogue worn by Wadlow. 1501 Pike Pl Seattle, WA 98101 ( Map It ) Map It ) --> Map It ) --> Connect & Follow Entertainment & Attractions --> Previous Mee Sum Pastry Next Secret Garden

Pam never paints the same design twice, which means every stone is a one-of-a-kind piece of art. The mandala stones are coated with epoxy resin making them strong, and safe to display outdoors. The mandala is a spiritual symbol in Buddhist culture. Translated from Sanskrit, mandala means “circle.” Since the circle has no beginning or end, mandalas are used as a visual representation of the universe. Often used to focus on while meditating, the mandala is also said to be reflective of the inner self. The belief is that by entering the mandala and proceeding towards its center, you are guided through the cosmic process of transforming the universe or self from a state of suffering into one of joy and happiness. “Of course, whether you meditate or not, they are a lovely piece of art and a truly special and unique gift for almost anyone,” Pam says. Pam has been selling her art at Pike Place Market for over 40 years.

Contact us through tinyfairyhouses.com . About Us Are you looking for something whimsical and completely unique? Kristi Ringger’s handmade ceramic fairy houses might exactly be what you’re looking for. She has been “bringing home the bacon” for The Market Foundation since 1986, raising more than $200,000 and counting. Legend has it that if you rub Rachel’s snout and make a donation, you’ll have good luck! Find Rachel the Piggy Bank underneath the Market’s famous Public Market Center clock and sign at the corner of Pike Street and Pike Place. Fun Facts Rachel arrived at the corner of Pike Place in 1986. She is a bronze cast piggy bank created by Whidbey Island sculptor Georgia Gerber. Weighing in at 550 pounds (250 kg), Rachel was named after a real 750-pound pig who won the 1985 Island County Fair. Her cousin, Billie the Piggy Bank, arrived in the Market in 2011 and currently sits on the Pike Place MarketFront. Guests may make an in-person reservation up to two weeks in advance, creating more time to explore the Market and less time waiting in line. About Us The story of Starbucks begins in 1971 along the cobblestone streets of Seattle’s historic Pike Place Market. It was here where Starbucks opened its first store, offering fresh-roasted coffee beans, tea and spices from around the world for its customers to take home. Their name was inspired by the classic tale Moby-Dick , evoking the seafaring tradition of the early coffee traders. Over the next 50 years, they would grow to open stores globally and welcome millions of customers each week, becoming a part of the fabric of tens of thousands of neighborhoods all around the world. In everything they do, Starbucks employees remain dedicated to their mission: to inspire and nurture the human spirit – one person, one cup, and one neighborhood at a time. Founded in 1912, the bakery is one of the oldest businesses in Pike Place Market. First selling in the Corner Market building facing Pike Street and later moving to the Sanitary Market next to Jack’s Fish Spot. Three Girls Bakery was also the first business licensed to women in the city of Seattle. Current owner Jacob Levy has a Market story as well. Jacob has worked in Pike Place Market for over 50 years. He started working at his father’s produce stand in 1966 and in 1979, Jacob and his sister Zelda bought Three Girls Bakery. At their pastry kitchen in Ballard, they create all the lovely pastries and cookies you can see through their large display cases. Imagine a Woolworth’s or an old Five and Dime, then imagine it run by the Addams family. That’s the Orange Dracula! Back when Chad was a teenager, he would hang out with his punk rock pals at these shops where they would find the weirdest stuff. “We got our pictures taken in the photo booth, ate at the lunch counter, and treasured our unusual finds. Not many novelty stores remain and today’s ‘dollar stores’ just aren’t as much fun, so I created Orange Dracula,” Chad said. Orange Dracula has a real old-fashioned photo booth, pinball, a vintage Pac-Man, and a HUGE selection of buttons, sundries, horror, pop culture, punk, goth, and just plain fun novelty items. Hang out, play some pinball, and check out all their groovy stuff. She had been designing and making toys for friends for many years, and after absentmindedly doodling a Donut Cat she wanted to see if she could successfully assemble one out of fabric. That very first Donut Cat, created on a whim, was crudely made and not nearly as cute as its modern-day descendants. But it nevertheless found a place within people’s hearts and before we knew it, we were making more of the funny felines for friends and family queueing up with money in hand. The following year we exhibited at our first craft show and were juried into Pike Place Market as daystall vendors. In November of 2019, after six years of setting up our booth in the crafts area of the market, we opened our flagship brick and mortar store! Today we peddle plush and propagate the idea that handmade is always best. The Donut Cat remains a pillar of our brand as we dream up new and exciting designs. He first made biscuits with his grandmother in rural North Carolina when he was about four years old. After he helped her make the biscuits for dinner, she would give him dough to make into biscuit-shaped animals. For years, Stone has tried different recipes and techniques to try to match his grandmother’s biscuit-making skills. After the past six months of perfecting his own recipe, he believes he may be finally catching up to her. He is trying to respect his grandmother’s legacy while injecting his own life experience, traveling and living in different places, to take biscuits to the next level. Head to the MarketFront off Western Avenue and grab one of their fried chicken Butterhole Biscuit Sandwiches. rows.name: Folio: The Seattle Athenaeum
rows.blurb: Folio is a non-profit member supported library and cultural center offering cultural and civic conversations, book and art discussions, intimate concerts, a circulating collection of donated books, and accessible work spaces with beautiful views at the heart of the historic Pike Place Market.

_page.text: 21 September 6:30 pm - 8:30 pm FOLIO PRESENTS – The Shape-Shifters: Tara Campbell, Ren Cedar Fuller, and G.G. Silverman Organizer Folio: The Seattle Athenaeum Phone (206) 330-4913 Email Caroline@FolioSeattle.org Website http://FolioSeattle.org Learn More Location Folio: The Seattle Athenaeum 93 Pike St. #307 Website https://FolioSeattle.org Category In-Person Event Literary Event More Info Learn More Folio: The Seattle Athenaeum is delighted to welcome local authors, G.G. Silverman ( The Blood Year Daughter ), Ren Cedar Fuller ( Bigger ), and Tara Campbell ( All the Wayward Angels ) for an exploration of all the ways we can morph and change. Through entirely different literary lenses and genres, the authors map the ways we shape-shift to carve out room for our own survival and agency. They act as a collective mirror, inviting audience members to consider the ‘ shapeshifter ‘ they have had to become, and discuss how they’ve bent their environments, bodies, and realities to fit their true selves. Tara Campbell is a writer, teacher, Kimbilio Fellow, and fiction co-editor at Barrelhouse. She teaches flash and speculative fiction, and is the author of two novels, two hybrid collections, and two short story collections. Nestled in a 1908 bathroom, Ghost Alley isn’t your conventional coffee shop. In this small, intimate, and definitely haunted nook, you can find the talented staff brewing up some of the best coffee in Seattle. Located underneath the iconic Public Market Center sign, Ghost Alley Espresso offers unique beverages in an intimate setting. They showcase small roasters in the Pacific Northwest, leading with Middle Fork Roaster’s full city roast. Drinks are prepared on a Modbar espresso machine, a uniquely efficient device that separates the heavy machinery below the counter, removing the barrier disruption to customers often presented with a standard countertop machine and inviting them closer to the barista process. The shop offers freshly roasted local coffee beans are for sale in addition to their crafty beverage lineup, delivered to the shop by bicycle every Tuesday. Under the original name of the Municipal Fish Market, City Fish Co. opened in 1918 in one of the original stalls on Pike Place. Immediately, throngs of consumers swooped down on the business, buying their three and half-pound limit of fish and oysters at a third of the previous cost. They sold over 1,391 pounds of salmon alone on that first day to hungry Seattleites. City Fish Co.’s opening followed a year of hardship for the nation. She has slowly developed her unique style and built her career as an abstract and mixed media painter, exploring a multitude mediums over the years. Her work explores her love of life, the city, and all that it encompasses: texture, simplicity, complexity, movement, color, spontaneity, awareness, and chaos. Their pickled peppers and vegetables deliver a crunchy, fresh explosion that will awaken your taste buds. By using farm-fresh ingredients and jarring them up within 24 hours, you can always count on a quality product. Bonnie B’s sources all of their produce from single-family organic farms in Washington State, including the organically grown Hungarian Wax pepper, which is used exclusively for its consistent heat level, great pepper flavor, and support of sustainable farming practices. This business is a true example of turning lemons into lemonade, loving family above all else, and hard work returning reward.
